title: Consider That Into Smoke It Turns...
text:
Consider that into smoke it turns,

the sweet good of your greatest contentment,

and human glory and the strongest pleasure

live scarcely one swift moment.


Such is man's immutable fate:

never to satisfy his anxious thought,

and at the price of his eagerness and torment

to acquire the rest of death.


Death, sad, pale, and divine,

awaits us at the end of our years

as the faithful wife awaits the unfaithful husband;


and by the ray of faith that lights her,

as austere as she appears to the wicked,

to the just man she presents herself beautiful.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the moral sonnet's contrast between fleeting pleasure and death illuminated by faith.

title: Let Them Close My Eyes with Grapes...
text:
Let them close my eyes with grapes.

(Transparent, deep fullness of curves.)


Let a blaze of apples wrap me.


Let them wrap me -omen of pulp-

in plums of perfumed touch...


Flood me

in a high tide of petals and trills.


Let them gird me -gird me!- with blue ecliptics.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem's ritual abundance of fruit, touch, petals, birdsong, and celestial curves.

title: To Stay Here Still, Germ...
text:
To stay here still, germ

of the coming song

-whole, virgin, future.


To stay asleep -intimate-

in the tender absent beating

of a deep secret presence.


And ecstasy -nourishment-

of the ignorant one -absent, pure-

unborn of clarities,

with the initial word

and the sweet intact tomorrow.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the unborn, future-tense stillness of the poem's germinal song.

title: Heaven Held Hostage
text:
I look at you without ceasing to contemplate you,

flake of sun, conjured foam,

and I open my heart from side to side

to offer you joyful entrance.


I understand that the slender light

was torn from chaos; I do not know by what art

I can carve you in a single petal

with light fingers, the delicacy of a fairy.


Again the spring of beauty

sets itself running with tranquil bearing,

counting its purity pearl by pearl.


Heaven held hostage, majesty without court;

wherever your head shines on high,

there is the sunflower, there its north.




1951
editorial_note: The translation keeps the sonnet's courtly praise and the dated closing line.

title: Nocturne
text:
What is your name, night of this night?

Tell me your name. Leave me

your sign and password

so that I may recognize you

always

through other different nights.


You offer me her forehead in half-moon

(half-moon of flesh),

her lips (pulp in shadow)

and her profile to the touch...

(Tomorrow my right hand

will play at drawing her outline in the air.)


What is your name, night of this night?

Tell me your name, leave me

your sign and password

so that I may recognize you

always

through other different nights.

And so I may call you joyfully,

trembling,

by your name!
editorial_note: The translation keeps the nocturne's repeated request for the night's name and sensual password.
